question.prompt: Design a distributed Key-Value Store with high availability and fault tolerance.
expectedPoints: Consistent hashing with virtual nodes to distribute keys across nodes
Data replication strategy across N nodes (preference lists)
Quorum consensus (R + W > N) for tunable consistency
Gossip protocol for decentralized node failure detection
commonMistakes: Centralized coordinator creating a single point of failure
Not discussing network partitions or CAP theorem trade-offs
Ignoring conflict resolution for concurrent writes

transcript: Candidate: For a distributed key-value store, we want horizontal scalability and high availability. To distribute keys evenly across cluster nodes without re-hashing everything when nodes join or leave, we use consistent hashing with virtual nodes on a hash ring. For replication, each key is replicated across the next N physical nodes clockwise on the ring. For consistency, we use quorum reads and writes: with replication factor N=3, we can configure R=2 and W=2 so R + W > N guarantees at least one node in the read quorum has the latest write. We can use a gossip protocol between nodes to detect heartbeat failures. For disk storage on each node, an LSM-tree with write-ahead log gives fast write performance. The part I am less certain about is how to resolve split-brain conflicts if two writes happen during a network partition—probably vector clocks or last-write-wins with timestamps.
notes: Well-structured Dynamo-style architecture. Explains consistent hashing, quorum formula, and LSM-tree. Weak on conflict resolution specifics.
